_comment: DESIGN.md §3, §8, §9. Waves 1-25 authored; the scaling factors apply only past wave 25, which the Final Showdown makes academic. Boss waves carry only their escort here - the boss is drawn from bossBank at run time (§3.4). All placeholders.

showdown._comment: §3.3, replaced. The attrition endgame is gone. The last monster wave is afterWave; clearing it moves every surviving army into the cross arena for a free-for-all. approachDepth is the open ground between a player's build grid and the centre square, so a spoke is buildZone.depth + approachDepth long and the centre is buildZone.width on a side. dampening scales healing, summon HP and crowd-control durations down by perSecond per second once graceSeconds have passed, so a fight cannot run forever. All placeholders.

centre._comment: KING OF THE HILL. Whichever army has the MOST living bodies inside the centre square holds it, and every one of that army’s bodies - wherever it is standing - deals damageDealt more damage and takes damageTaken less. A tie is held by everyone tied, so contesting it is never worse than conceding it. Without this the arena rewards exactly one strategy: mass the slowest, longest-ranged units you can afford, let the other three fight, and walk in to mop up. A reason to stand in the middle is a reason to own a front line. Percentages, in the same convention as an ability’s modify effect: 0.5 is +50%, -0.5 is -50%.

showdown._sightNote: LINE OF SIGHT. The arena is a cross, and the four corners of its bounding square are not arena: nothing stands there and nothing walks there. With this on they are not transparent either - a body cannot shoot through one, so the back of the south spoke cannot draw a bead on the back of the east spoke across the gap between them. Off, the corners are glass, and a long enough gun covers two spokes from a standing start while nothing can walk to it. A switch rather than a constant so the difference can be measured rather than assumed.

acquire._comment: How far a unit looks for something to fight in the arena, edge to edge in tiles: its own reach plus margin, never less than minimum. Nothing looks across the whole board - a unit with nothing inside this walks at the centre instead, which is what makes four armies converge rather than each pick a duel from thirty tiles away. The lane's equivalent is lane.monsterAcquireRange. Placeholders.

showdown._walkNote: Every body walks walkSpeed times its lane speed in the arena. Lane speeds are set for holding a line, and at 0.2 to 0.65 tiles a second a tile of reach was three to five seconds of shooting at something that could not answer: an army of nothing but rung 6 won 176 of 176 fights against every other shape its own builder could field, most of them with nine bodies of ten still standing. At 2.5 the best shapes are a swarm, a rung 3 and 4 core and the designed spread, all within five points of each other, and rung 6 on its own wins 45%. Faster than that and the swarm takes the centre before anything can shoot it.

endless._comment: Solo mode's last wave, in place of the Final Showdown (§3.3, solo). After the last authored wave and one more build phase, the field fills to maxConcurrentMonsters at once and stays full: every monster that dies is replaced on the next tick, each a type drawn at random from every monster the waves used. Every bossEverySeconds a batch of bosses falls due - firstBosses in the first, one more every bossGrowthEvery batches - and they take the next places that free up. Every stepSeconds the stream climbs one wave of the growth curve (scaling). Nothing can be bought once it opens and a fallen unit stays down: only sends are still open. The match ends when the fortress falls; the score is the monsters killed.

_poolsNote: §8.1, amended: a lane has two pools on the field, not one. maxConcurrentMonsters caps what the wave brought (and solo's endless stream, bosses included); maxConcurrentSends caps what was sent at the lane. Each pool's overflow waits in the reserve and enters as a body OF THE SAME POOL dies, so sends never queue behind the wave and the wave never queues behind sends. Equal on purpose: a full wave and a full complement of sends can be on the field at once, sixty bodies, and the perf harness (npm run perf) and the wire harness (npm run wire) measure exactly that.

enrage._comment: Additive, not compounding: multiplier = 1 + ratePerSecond * secondsEnraged. rate 0.03 is derived from the doc's worked example (60s in = 2.8x). Applies to monster damage, move speed and attack speed - never to HP.

_combinationsNote: THE SIXTEEN. Every armor with every damage type, and the monster a wave of that pair is made of. Waves 1-4, 6-9, 11-14 and 16-19 are each ONE of these, all of it, every pair once a match, in an order shuffled by the seed (waves.ts `combinationOrder`). A wave of three kinds asked nothing of an army - a general-purpose army beat any mixture - so players stopped countering; a wave that is all Plate dealing all Pierce asks one question, and the preview tells everyone what it is thirty seconds early.
_lateWavesNote: Waves 21 to 24 are two of the sixteen each, half and half: the eight that took the biggest share of the surviving armies' health in the combination waves, shuffled into four pairs, decided as wave 20 ends (waves.ts `chooseLateWaves`, tick.ts). The table's `count` is the whole wave, both halves.
_clockNote: DESIGN CHANGE to §3.2: there is no global wave-spawn clock. The only global timers are this 30s build phase and the enrage clock (§8). Combat runs until every living lane is empty, so a second wave can never land on an unfinished one.
_compositionNote: §9.1, REPLACED: a table, not a curve. One row a wave: `count` monsters at `scale` times their written health and damage, or on a boss wave one boss at `bossScale` - alone, no escort. A boss is drawn from the bank so that the four boss waves before the last bring each boss once (waves.ts `bossFor`). Wave 25 is authored: the council of bosses, as before. `armyGold` is what the wave is tuned to be beaten by (docs/BALANCE.md).
